clue.text: Raced around first man flipping fast

indicators.note: the word for raced sits on either side of the reversed first man

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to race

indicators.note: flipping turns the first man's name back to front

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone sprints off as the first man does a somersault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like the adjective for speed, matching 'raced', but here it is the noun for a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic holy month of daytime fasting, so it is a fast.

clue.text: Class following school subject write again

indicators.note: the word for class comes after the school subject, so it is placed second

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
a type is a class or kind

explanation.surface: A student whose class follows a lesson has to write out their work again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, a subject on the British school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype a document is to key it in a second time, a synonym for writing it again.

clue.text: Ill-will displayed by a student prodding rodents

indicators.note: the letters for a student are poked into the middle of the rodents

parts.note: mice are small rodents
taken as written
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A student cruelly pokes at some rodents in a lab, showing spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spiteful intent to harm, the same as ill-will or animosity.

clue.text: Delicate claim I'd opt to alter

indicators.note: altering these letters rearranges them into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they will opt to change a sensitive claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic approach is tactful, handling a sensitive matter delicately.

clue.text: Asian region in north-eastern China

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a pal

explanation.surface: A geographical note placing an Asian region in the north-east of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country, but it is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country in South Asia, so it counts as an Asian region.

clue.text: Ancient, boring aristocrat dressed down

indicators.note: the aristocrat's letters are bored through by the word for ancient

parts.note: toff is British slang for an upper-class person
old is a plain synonym for ancient

explanation.surface: A dull old nobleman turned up in casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed down' suggests casual clothing, but it means reprimanded. A toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being told off is being scolded, the idiomatic sense of being dressed down.

clue.text: Rottenness eerily overwhelms this state

indicators.note: the two words swamp the answer, holding it inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A spooky decay engulfs a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA, and the hiding phrase points to it as this state.

clue.text: Departed from school at eleven

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of school, the whole of at and the start of eleven

explanation.surface: A child leaves school at the age of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Late is a euphemism for dead, as in 'the late king', and departed is another word for the dead.

clue.text: Oscar knocked over bad kind of paint, a greasy liquid

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in this down clue the word for bad is read upwards

parts.note: evil is a strong word for bad
oil paint, as used by artists

explanation.surface: Oscar spills a pot of awful paint, leaving an oily mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is the fat pressed from olives, a liquid that is greasy to the touch.

clue.text: Sensations of ecstasy repeatedly during affairs

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: flings are brief romantic affairs
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
repeatedly says the ecstasy letter comes again, so it is written a second time

explanation.surface: Feelings of rapture happen again and again in love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: EE sits inside FLINGS, after FL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings are sensations, things felt physically or emotionally.

clue.text: Oddly thug, with impudence, makes bloomer

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word thug

parts.note: taken as written
lip is cheeky backchat

explanation.surface: An odd scene of a cheeky thug making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring flower, and in crosswords a bloomer is anything that blooms.

clue.text: Bargain over rubbish kind of suit

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for bargain is read backwards

parts.note: a snip is British slang for a bargain
tripe is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A shopper haggles about a suit they think is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for something very cheap, a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe suit is cut from cloth with fine vertical lines, a classic business style.

clue.text: Spooner's shortage of pastries is a total fabrication

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two parts are exchanged

parts.note: a lack of something is a shortage of it
pies are baked pastry dishes

explanation.surface: Someone claims a pie shortage is pure invention.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner swaps the opening sounds: 'lack of pies', with 'of' said as 'ov', comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack of lies is an idiom for a story that is completely untrue, wholly made up.

clue.text: Openers for Sussex edgily missing in match

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the four following words are taken

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sussex's opening batsmen nervously miss out in a game; Sussex is an English county cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' suggests the batsmen who open a cricket innings, but here it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is short for semi-final, the match played before the final in a tournament.

clue.text: A Parisian pudding's brought up chilled

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: brought up means raised, so in this down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: read as puddings, plural, which are desserts

explanation.surface: A Parisian's pudding is served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilled' points to the pudding being cold, but it is the slang sense of relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstressed means free of tension, the same as being chilled, slang for relaxed and calm.

clue.text: Perhaps Ms Vorderman's drunk gin twice — it's a Christmas activity

parts.note: Carol Vorderman is a British TV presenter, so her first name with 's gives Carol's

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: twice says the rearranged gin comes a second time, so it is written again

explanation.surface: A TV presenter has had a couple of gins at a festive party.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol Vorderman is a British TV presenter, so 'Perhaps' marks Carol as an example name. CAROLS, then GIN rearranged as ING, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol singing is the seasonal custom of going round singing Christmas songs.

clue.text: Cracks running over European ships

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word for running sits above the rest

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: Fissures run across Europe's ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' looks like fractures, but here it means jokes, as in wisecracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and one-liners are short jokes of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Dispatched to stop a worker, maybe a no-show

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for dispatched plugs the gap in a and the worker, as a stopper does

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee
sent is a synonym for dispatched

explanation.surface: An employee is sent out to block a worker who may not have turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the standard crossword shorthand for a worker bee or ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee fails to appear where expected, just like a no-show at an appointment.

clue.text: Slobbish person raised capital in European country

parts.note: a sloven is someone untidy and lazy

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in this down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, its digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A slob is promoted to power in a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, but it is the old adjective for excellent, A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe, so it is a European country.

clue.text: Combative people confused e.g. Ben Stiller

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are used, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Hostile people bewildered someone like the actor Ben Stiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerents are those engaged in fighting or eager to, a synonym for combative people.

clue.text: A large college hosting 1,000 students once

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the college holds the thousand inside it, as a host contains a guest

parts.note: uni is short for university
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A big college has room for a thousand pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former pupils of a school or university, people who were students in the past.

clue.text: King cutting some bananas for a meal

indicators.note: the king's letter cuts into the middle of the bananas

parts.note: bananas grow and are sold in a bunch
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king slices bananas to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning combination of breakfast and lunch, a meal in itself.

clue.text: English sailors ignoring a reason to go green?

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: the navy is a body of sailors
taken as written

explanation.surface: English sailors overlook an argument for environmental policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go green' suggests becoming eco-friendly, but it refers to being green with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'green with envy' makes jealousy the thing that turns a person green.

clue.text: Moving around, I recall new location of Bordeaux?

indicators.note: moving letters around rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remembers relocating to a new place in Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux' looks like the French city, but it is the wine named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottles of claret such as Bordeaux are stored in a cellar, so that is where the wine is kept.

clue.text: Admission made by watchman losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for watchman goes

parts.note: a sentry is a guard on watch

explanation.surface: A guard confesses after being beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry means the right to go in, which is what admission to a place grants.

clue.text: Look and glimpse Mike

parts.note: to glimpse something is to see it briefly
Mike is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to look and catch sight of Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to appear a certain way, as in 'you look tired', the verb sense of look.

clue.text: Most kind-hearted offer is translated into French

parts.note: to tender is to offer formally, as with a tender for a contract
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: A generous proposal is rendered into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderest is the superlative of tender, meaning gentlest and most caring, so the most kind-hearted.

clue.text: Simple fellow is retiring before start of week

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Monday, abbreviated Mon, is the day that starts the working week

explanation.surface: A shy simpleton has a quiet weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme character Simple Simon makes the name a fellow linked with simplicity.

clue.text: Renaissance man's calculations are written the wrong way

indicators.note: writing letters the wrong way round reverses them

parts.note: sums are arithmetical calculations
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Renaissance scholar's arithmetic is set down backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was a Dutch humanist scholar, a leading figure of the Northern Renaissance.

clue.text: Language homework returned before meal

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's own home
a dish is a course or meal

explanation.surface: Schoolwork is handed back before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homework' looks like school work, but it is DIY, repairs done around the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is the historic tongue of Ashkenazi Jews, a Germanic language written in Hebrew script.
